to be offered. And not the Great Litanies and Prayers.
At Midday, you shall say the three [hymns of] "Have Mercy" [Voghormya].
After that: Hymn of Rest, and [the litany] "For the Souls" [Hogvots].
And in the Evening: "Bow down [your ear]" [Khonarhëtso] and "Live" [Apreto].
Mesedi: "The mouth of the righteous." Verse: "Fret not."
Book of Genesis 1:1: "In the beginning God created," to verse 3:24: "of the tree of life."
Proverbs 1:1: "To know wisdom," to verse 9: "upon your neck."
Prophet Isaiah 40:1: "Comfort ye," to verse 8: "stands forever."
And then say: "Let [my prayer] be set forth."
Litany: "Let us beseech."
"Holy God," who didst come and [art to come].
Hymn at Evening [Hambartsi] Tone 3 [b3]: "Who from nothingness."
Litany: "For the peace."
Prayer: "Merciful Father."
Psalm 64 [65]: "Hear us." Verse: "Praise is due to thee."
Gospel according to Matthew 20:17: "And Jesus going up," to verse 28: "a ransom for many."
Litany: "Let us beseech," "Save."
Prayer: "King [of peace]."

Great Tuesday. Tone Plagal 2 [bk]: "The wise virgins," with its canons [sarok’n].
Morning Song: "They shall be brought to the king." Verse: "They shall be brought with gladness."
Psalm 44 [45]: "They shall be brought to the king." Verse: "My heart hath poured forth."
Gospel according to Mark 12:13: "And they send unto him some," to verse 44: "all her living."
Then [the hymn] "Of the Creator" [Ararchakan], and "Save."
Prayer: "To thy almighty and wondrous coming."
And in the Evening: "Bow down [your ear]" [Khonarhëtso] and "Live" [Apreto].
Mesedi: "Thou hast dealt in goodness." Verse: "Good art thou, O Lord."
Book of Genesis 6:9: "These are the generations," to verse 9:17: "which is upon the earth."
Proverbs 9:1: "Wisdom hath builded," to verse 10:6: "untimely mourning."
Prophet Isaiah 40:9: "Get thee up into a high mountain," to verse 17: "are counted to him."
"Holy God," who didst come and art to come.
Hymn at Evening [Hambartsi] Tone 3 [b3]: "Grant us, O Lord."
After the "Merciful Father", Psalm 24 [25], in a mournful voice, say in full: "To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up."
And while saying it, they shall vest ten children, and place in their hands burning candles, in the likeness of the ten virgins, who shall come and stand before the Gospel.
Gospel according to Matthew 24:1 [through to chapter 25], and going out, to verse 26:2: "is betrayed to be crucified."
Litany: "Let us beseech," "Save."
Prayer: "King of peace."

Great Wednesday. Tone Plagal 3 [g3]: "He who on the throne of glory," with its canons.
Morning Song: "They thought and spoke." Verse: "They set [their mouth] against heaven."
Psalm 40 [41], in a mournful voice, say in full: "He who did eat of my bread." Verse: "Blessed is he that considereth."
Gospel according to Mark 14:1: "After two days was the feast of the passover," to verse 11: "how he might betray him."
[The hymn] "Of the Creator" [Ararchakan].
Litany: "Let us beseech," "Save."
Prayer: "To thy almighty and wondrous coming."
And in the Evening: "Bow down [your ear]" [Khonarhëtso] and "Live" [Apreto].
Mesedi: "Look upon me and hear." Verse: "How long, O Lord."
Book of Genesis 18:1: "And God appeared to him," to verse 19:30: "his daughters with him."
Proverbs 1:10: "My son, let them not deceive thee," to verse 19: "they destroy their own lives."
Prophet Zechariah 11:11: "And the Canaanites knew," to verse 14: "between Israel."
Litany: "Let us pray."
"Holy God," who didst come and art to come.
Hymn at Evening [Hambartsi] Tone Plagal 3 [g3]: "New wonders."
After the "Merciful Father", Psalm 40 [41], in a mournful voice: "I said: Lord [have mercy on me]." Verse: "Blessed is he."
Gospel according to Matthew 26:3: "Then assembled together," to verse 16: "to betray him unto them."
Litany: "Let us beseech," "Save."
Prayer: "King of peace."

Great Thursday. Tone Plagal 3 [g3]: "He who exaltest," with its canons.
Morning Song: "They hunted." Verse: "But the Lord was."
Magnificat [Mankunk] Tone 1 [ak]: "Today was set up."
Litany: "For peace."
Prayer: "Holy art thou, O Lord."
Psalm 93 [94], in a mournful voice. Antiphon: "They hunted." Verse: "O God of vengeance."
Gospel according to John 12:27: "Now is my soul troubled," to verse 43: "more than the glory of God."
Litany: "Let us beseech," "Save."
Prayer: "To thy almighty and wondrous coming."

And at the third hour, they shall gather at the church door for the dismissal of the penitents; whether there be any or not, the service must be performed.
But first: "Blessed be the Holy Spirit, true God." Psalm by number: "Have mercy on me, O God" [Psalm 50 [51]].
